cityWatch.text: Karnataka plans to appeal the High Court ruling on its enhanced SC/ST quota and ask the Prime Minister to include the hike in the Constitution’s Ninth Schedule.

lead.headline: WOMAN PRESUMED MURDERED TURNS UP ALIVE AFTER MAN SPENT 2.6 YEARS IN JAIL
lead.deck: A woman reported missing in Mandya in 2019 returned this week. Police say they have reopened the case; the man charged with her murder was released on bail in 2024.
paragraphs: A construction worker spent 2.6 years in prison after being charged with murdering Manju N, who disappeared from Pandavapura in 2019. She returned alive on November 11, exposing major gaps in the investigation.

Police had relied on a call she made from the worker’s phone before she went missing. He said he had lent it to a stranger at a bus stand and denied knowing her. He was released on bail in February 2024.

Manju told reporters she had eloped and did not know a murder case had been filed. Police say she is now at a women’s support centre and that they will investigate the case; her lawyer has informed the court.

sidebarStory.headline: IAF WING COMMANDER ACCUSED OF SHARING WAR PLANS WITH PAKISTANI OPERATIVE
sidebarStory.subhead: A Delhi police chargesheet alleges that classified deployment, drone and aircraft details were sent to a suspected intelligence operative.
paragraphs: Police allege the officer shared war-plan documents, drone capabilities, military deployment locations and details of frontline aircraft movements. The chargesheet says the disclosures risked exposing operational vulnerabilities.
Investigators also allege the officer installed spyware on devices used by five subordinates. The case is being prosecuted under the Official Secrets Act.

groups.ariaLabel: Bengaluru and Karnataka local employment, infrastructure and crime news

stories.headline: LOCALS SEEK TRANSPARENT HIRING DATA AT KEMPEGOWDA AIRPORT
paragraphs: A Kannada organisation has asked for a clear assessment of how many Kannadigas work across Kempegowda International Airport and its contractors.
Bangalore International Airport Ltd said it is engaging with authorities and stakeholders after representatives sought stronger local recruitment.

stories.headline: STATE SEEKS TO BLACKLIST L&T OVER DELAYS AFFECTING 388 HABITATIONS
paragraphs: Rural Development Minister Eshwar Khandre directed officials to blacklist Larsen & Toubro over delays to a drinking-water project serving 388 habitations in Dharwad and Belagavi districts.
The project is meant to bring water from the Renukasagar reservoir. Officials were also told to issue final notices to other contractors that have missed deadlines.

stories.headline: ONE ACCUSED IN WHITEFIELD LAWYER’S MURDER HELD IN BIHAR
paragraphs: Police arrested Amit Kumar Dubey in Bihar in connection with the October killing of Bengaluru advocate B Manjunath.
The prime suspect, accused of shooting the 43-year-old lawyer, remained at large in the latest police update.

groups.ariaLabel: India national security, public health and conflict news

stories.headline: FOUR KILLED IN SUSPECTED MILITANT ATTACK ON TWO CARS
paragraphs: Two men and two women were killed when suspected militants fired on two vehicles in Manipur’s Ukhrul district, police said.
The shooting took place on the Imphal–Ukhrul road, a day after a woman was killed in a separate attack in the state.

stories.headline: CAPITAL’S AIR FORECAST TO STAY VERY POOR THROUGH WEEKEND
paragraphs: Delhi’s AQI settled at 373 on Friday evening after several stations recorded severe pollution earlier in the day.
The Air Quality Early Warning System expects very poor air to persist through November 16, keeping health concerns high across the capital.

stories.headline: PROBE UNDER WAY AFTER FORGED COURT ORDERS LED TO 129 SITE BLOCKS
paragraphs: India is investigating how telecom officials were persuaded to block 129 betting websites using court orders that investigators say were forged.
Police have sought ministry records as part of the inquiry into documents presented in the names of the Rajasthan and Allahabad High Courts.

groups.ariaLabel: India trade policy, industry and justice news

stories.headline: US ASSURES INDIA A TARIFF EDGE OVER RIVALS IN PROPOSED TRADE DEAL
paragraphs: US negotiators have assured India that a proposed bilateral trade agreement will give Indian goods a comparative tariff advantage over competing countries, a senior government official said.
The two countries are continuing talks on the first phase of the deal, with parts of the customs and trade-facilitation chapter reported resolved.

stories.headline: CENTRE ORDERS PROBE AFTER ADANI PROJECT COST CUT BY 99%
paragraphs: The Centre has ordered a probe after Adani Green Energy revised the estimated cost of its 1,500-MW Tarali pumped-storage project from ₹5,675 crore to ₹56.75 crore.
The revision also sharply reduced the proposed wildlife conservation deposit, prompting scrutiny of the changed estimate.

stories.headline: COURT ORDERS NARCO AND POLYGRAPH TESTS FOR ACTOR IN MURDER PROBE
paragraphs: A Dehradun court ordered actor Urmila Sanawar to undergo narco-analysis and polygraph examinations over an audio recording that refers to a “VIP” in connection with the 2022 murder of 19-year-old Ankita Bhandari.
The order concerns a new line of inquiry into the high-profile case.

stories.headline: MICROSOFT OUTAGE DISRUPTS AIRLINE SUPPORT AS RECOVERY CONTINUES
paragraphs: Microsoft said it was gradually restoring traffic in parts of its Asia-Pacific infrastructure, including India, after Outlook, Teams and other services were disrupted for a second day.
SpiceJet cancelled three Delhi departures and two others were delayed; IndiGo said its email support was affected while flight operations continued.

listing: Storytelling, workshops and family events are scheduled around Bengaluru today.
KLES Diabetes Centre in Belagavi begins a week of screening and diabetes education.

stories.headline: PARTLY CLOUDY TODAY; NO CITY WARNING IN FORCE

paragraphs: The India Meteorological Department forecasts partly cloudy skies for Bengaluru on Saturday, with a minimum of 16°C and maximum of 30°C. No warning is in force.
